# opskit

> A personal operating system in a folder of plaintext. Markdown files in the user's own git repo hold knowledge (wiki), tasks, and a journal; one `ops <verb>` command is the only writer. Two faces, one door: humans use `ops ui` (a guided terminal UI generated from the machine contract), agents and scripts use `ops <verb> --json` (a frozen envelope + exit-code protocol). A guardrail classifies every invocation (read / safe_write / draft_only / confirm / deny); nothing transmits without a human. No server, no daemon, no cloud. Python 3.10+ stdlib engine; optional layers (semantic search, local models, backups, scheduled jobs, the compiled terminal UI) are opt-in via a layered installer.

Key facts: the repo is a TEMPLATE — `script/get` clones a private copy to `~/ops`, `script/setup` wires the machine, `script/update` 3-way-merges only engine files so user content is never touched. The generated `ops.json` (schema `ops.json/3`) describes the entire verb surface: args, output schemas, risk classes, per-action grammar (`actions[]` with typed args + completion providers), and capabilities. Exit codes are a protocol: 0 ok · 2 usage · 3 needs --yes · 4 not found · 5 denied — refusal messages carry the exact corrected command ("refusals teach"). `ops mcp` is a stateless MCP stdio server whose tool list is generated from ops.json; every tool call shells back through `ops <verb> --json`, so the guardrail and logs remain the single enforcement path. Four roots: `~/ops` (this repo), `~/work` (code, separate repos), `~/files` (binary assets, restic-backed), `~/dotfiles`.

All links below are raw markdown — fetch them directly.

## Start here

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/README.md): what opskit is, quick start, the verb surface, guardrail classes, agent wiring, project layout
- [Layered setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/setup.md): the `ops setup` installer — wizard, dashboard, all six layers (skeleton, search, backups, models, automation, ui), status enum, agent rules
- [Docs map](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/README.md): every doc, organized by reader intent

## The contracts (for agents)

- [Machine contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/machine-contract.md): the normative reference — `--json` envelope, exit-code protocol, `--dry-run` semantics, `ops.json/3` schema, `cmd.json` sidecar, `actions[]` grammar, completion contract
- [Agent contract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/AGENTS.md): the operating contract any agent reads before driving the vault
- [Operating manual](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/skills/operate-ops/SKILL.md): the detailed skill — orientation ritual, verb reference, provenance rules, what agents must never do

## Understanding the system

- [Architecture](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/architecture.md): why the system is shaped this way — principles, the one-door enforcement path, trade-offs, frontends
- [Decision log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/DECISIONS.md): the ADR record of every load-bearing decision, including rejected alternatives
- [Changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed and when

## Capabilities

- [The terminal UI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/terminal-ui.md): install, use, and update `ops ui` — the contract-generated human face, shipped as a compiled binary
- [Plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/plugins.md): write your own verbs against the frozen SDK; the install + trust model for packs
- [Backup & share](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/backup-and-share.md): the restic backup family (append-only cloud key) and capability-URL sharing
- [Agent-readable shares](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/share-agent-markdown.md): how a shared link serves raw markdown to any agent's fetch tool
- [Obsidian compatibility](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gabros20/opskit/main/docs/obsidian-compat.md): the normative emit/tolerate definition for the zero-cost frontend
